scenario: 语义搜索要在数百万文档里为一个 query 找到最相关结果，还要在几十毫秒内返回。
scenario_en: Semantic search must find the most relevant results for a query among millions of docs and return in tens of milliseconds.
q: 为什么工业级语义搜索几乎都用「两阶段」架构，两阶段各干什么？
q_en: Why do production semantic-search systems use a two-stage architecture, and what does each stage do?
why: 第一阶段用便宜检索器在百万库毫秒级捞候选（召回优先），第二阶段用昂贵但精准的 re-ranker 只精排 top-K。单靠精排跑全库延迟爆炸，单靠检索器精度不够，分工才能同时拿到速度和精度。
why_en: A cheap retriever pulls candidates from millions of docs in milliseconds, then an expensive re-ranker precisely scores only the top-K, so you get both speed and precision.
diagram:
flowchart LR Q["query"] --> R["① 检索器
百万库毫秒召回"] R --> F["融合候选
100–1000 篇"] F --> K["② re-ranker
精排 top-K"] K --> O["最终结果"]
options: 用一个昂贵精排模型给全库每篇文档逐一打分，牺牲延迟换全库最高精度，靠疯狂堆机器硬扛吞吐
两阶段跑同一个检索模型，第二阶段把 top-K 重跑几遍取平均来降低打分方差
先用便宜检索器毫秒级从百万文档捞候选，再用昂贵 re-ranker 只精排 top-K
第一阶段先精排全库、第二阶段再粗排收窄，精度层层放宽以省算力
options_en: Use one expensive re-ranker to score every doc in the corpus, trading latency for max precision and betting that piling on more hardware can absorb it.
Run the same retrieval model in both stages, re-running the top-K a few times and averaging to cut scoring variance.
First a cheap retriever pulls candidates from millions of docs in ms, then an expensive re-ranker precisely scores only the top-K.
Stage one precisely ranks the whole corpus, stage two coarsely narrows it, loosening precision layer by layer.
optionExplanations: 精排模型对每篇一次前向传播，全库百万篇跑一遍是秒级甚至分钟级，直接超时；加机器也补不回 O(N) 全库精排的成本。
重跑取平均降的是方差不是延迟，也没解决「全库打分太贵」这个根本矛盾，纯属浪费算力。
对；检索器负责召回（快、召回优先），re-ranker 负责精度（慢、只看 top-K），分工让系统同时拿到速度和精度。
顺序反了：全库精排正是两阶段架构要避免的昂贵操作，先精后粗把最贵的一步放在最费的位置。
optionExplanations_en: The re-ranker runs one forward pass per doc, so scoring millions takes seconds to minutes and times out; hardware cannot undo O(N) full-corpus scoring.
Re-running and averaging cuts variance not latency and never fixes the core problem that full-corpus scoring is too expensive.
Correct — the retriever handles recall (fast, recall-first) and the re-ranker handles precision (slow, top-K only), so the split gets both.
Backwards: full-corpus precise ranking is exactly what two-stage avoids, and precise-then-coarse puts the costliest step where it hurts most.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第一阶段从全库快速召回候选的模型，通常是 dual encoder 配 ANN 索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A retriever is the first-stage model that quickly recalls candidates from the full corpus, usually a dual encoder over an ANN index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第二阶段对少量候选做精细相关性打分的模型，通常是 cross-encoder。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A re-ranker is the second-stage model that finely scores a small candidate set, usually a cross-encoder.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第一阶段召回后送去精排的前 K 篇候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Top-K is the K best candidates from stage one that get passed to re-ranking.

q: 两阶段语义搜索里有哪三个核心架构决策？(多选)
q_en: What are the three core architectural decisions in two-stage semantic search? (multiple)
why: 这三个决策——dual encoder 选型、hybrid 融合、cross-encoder 精排——都被同一根轴（延迟 vs 精度）牵着走；前端渲染是产品层，不影响检索质量。
why_en: The three decisions — dual-encoder choice, hybrid fusion, and cross-encoder re-ranking — are all governed by the latency-versus-accuracy axis.
options: dual encoder 选型（DPR / E5 / BGE 等 dense 检索模型）
hybrid retrieval 融合（BM25 稀疏 + dense 稠密怎么合并候选）
cross-encoder re-ranking（top-K 精排模型与候选数 K）
用哪种前端框架渲染搜索结果页
options_en: Dual-encoder choice (dense retrieval models like DPR / E5 / BGE).
Hybrid retrieval fusion (how to merge BM25 sparse and dense candidates).
Cross-encoder re-ranking (the top-K re-ranker and the candidate count K).
Which front-end framework renders the results page.
optionExplanations: 对；dual encoder 决定第一阶段召回质量和索引成本，是 dense 检索的地基。
对；dense 会漏精确关键词，hybrid 把 BM25 和 dense 候选融合，决定召回的完整性。
对；cross-encoder 决定精度上限，K 决定你在延迟-精度曲线上的位置。
错；渲染是前端产品层，和检索模型的延迟-精度权衡无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the dual encoder sets stage-one recall quality and index cost, the foundation of dense retrieval.
Correct — dense misses exact keywords, so hybrid fuses BM25 and dense candidates and governs recall completeness.
Correct — the cross-encoder sets the precision ceiling and K sets where you sit on the latency-precision curve.
Wrong — rendering is a front-end product layer, unrelated to the model's latency-accuracy tradeoff.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个独立 transformer 分别把 query 和 doc 编码成同维向量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dual encoder uses two separate transformers to encode query and doc into same-dimension vectors.

termDefinitions.meaning: 经典稀疏检索函数，按词频/逆文档频率给关键词匹配打分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BM25 (Best Matching 25) is a classic sparse retrieval function scoring keyword matches by term frequency and inverse document frequency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 query 和 doc 拼成一条序列过一个 transformer，让 token 互相 attend。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-encoder concatenates query and doc into one sequence through a transformer so tokens attend to each other.

scenario: 500 万篇文档的语义搜索，p99 要 <100ms，还得能命中 SKU 编号这类精确词。
scenario_en: Semantic search over 5M docs with a p99 under 100ms that must still hit exact tokens like SKU codes.

scenario: 你要设计 dense 检索第一阶段：怎么让「一个 query」和「百万篇 doc」都变成可比的向量。
scenario_en: You design the dense-retrieval first stage: how to turn one query and millions of docs into comparable vectors.
q: dual encoder（双塔）怎么做 dense 检索，相关性怎么算？
q_en: How does a dual encoder do dense retrieval, and how is relevance computed?
why: 两个独立 transformer 分别把 query、doc 编成同维向量，相关性用点积/余弦算。关键是 doc 向量离线预算好，query 来了只跑 query 编码器，再用 ANN 找最近邻，毫秒返回。
why_en: Two separate transformers encode query and doc into same-dim vectors scored by dot product or cosine, with doc vectors precomputed offline so only the query encoder runs at query time.
options: 一个 transformer 同时读入 query 和 doc 输出匹配分，每来一个 query 就把全库重编码一遍
两个独立 transformer 分别把 query、doc 编成同维向量，相关性用点积/余弦，doc 向量离线预算
把 query 和 doc 拼成一句话过 transformer，让每个 query token attend 每个 doc token
用倒排索引按关键词精确匹配，不需要向量，靠词频排序
options_en: One transformer reads query and doc together to output a match score, re-encoding the whole corpus for each query.
Two separate transformers encode query and doc into same-dim vectors scored by dot product/cosine, with doc vectors precomputed offline.
Concatenate query and doc into one sequence through a transformer so every query token attends every doc token.
Use an inverted index for exact keyword matching, no vectors, ranking by term frequency.
optionExplanations: 那是 cross-encoder 的做法，每个 query 都要重扫全库、O(N) 前向传播，第一阶段召回根本扛不住。
对；双塔的精髓是 query 塔和 doc 塔解耦，doc 向量离线算好进 ANN 索引，在线只算 query 一次。
拼接过一个 transformer 是 cross-encoder，精度高但太慢，只适合第二阶段精排少量候选。
倒排+词频是 BM25 稀疏检索，抓精确关键词但不懂语义，不是 dense dual encoder。
optionExplanations_en: That is the cross-encoder approach, re-scanning the whole corpus per query with O(N) forward passes — first-stage recall cannot bear it.
Correct — the dual encoder decouples the query and doc towers, precomputing doc vectors into an ANN index and encoding only the query online.
Concatenating through one transformer is a cross-encoder: accurate but too slow, fit only for re-ranking a few candidates in stage two.
Inverted index plus term frequency is BM25 sparse retrieval — great at exact keywords but blind to semantics, not a dense dual encoder.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两向量的点积/余弦相似度，值越大越相关，是 dense 检索的相关性分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dot product / cosine similarity between two vectors — higher means more relevant — is the dense-retrieval relevance score.

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻搜索：在向量索引里快速找与 query 向量最近的一批 doc，不用扫全库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) search quickly finds the doc vectors closest to a query vector without scanning the whole corpus.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用稠密向量表示 query 和 doc，靠向量相似度找相关文档。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dense retrieval represents query and doc as dense vectors and finds relevant docs by vector similarity.

scenario: 语料库几百万篇，语义搜索要 <50ms 返回，每天还有海量 query。
scenario_en: The corpus has millions of docs, search must return in under 50ms, and query volume is huge.
q: dual encoder 为什么能做到毫秒级召回？关键设计是什么？
q_en: Why can a dual encoder recall in milliseconds — what is the key design?
why: doc 向量离线预算好存进 ANN 索引，在线只跑 query 编码器一次，再用 ANN 近似最近邻毫秒取回候选。若在线还要现编码全库 doc，就退化成 O(N) 全库扫描，延迟爆炸。
why_en: Doc vectors are precomputed offline into an ANN index, so at query time only the query encoder runs once and ANN returns neighbors in milliseconds.
options: doc 向量离线预算进 ANN 索引，在线只编码 query 一次，毫秒取回最近邻
每来一个 query 就把全库 doc 实时重新编码一遍，再逐一算余弦相似度取最高的那批
把所有 doc 全文缓存在内存里，用字符串匹配代替向量运算加速
靠更大的 GPU 集群把全库精排的秒级延迟硬压到毫秒，算法本身不动
options_en: Doc vectors are precomputed into an ANN index; only the query is encoded online, returning neighbors in ms.
Re-encode the whole corpus in real time for every query, then compute cosine similarity one by one and take the top.
Cache all doc full text in memory and replace vector math with string matching to go faster.
Throw a bigger GPU cluster at it to force full-corpus re-ranking from seconds to milliseconds without changing the algorithm.
optionExplanations: 对；离线预算 + 在线只算 query + ANN 近似最近邻，是把「百万库」变成「毫秒召回」的三件套。
在线重编码全库就是 O(N) 全量前向传播，正是双塔要绕开的成本，延迟直接秒级。
字符串匹配丢掉了语义相似性，也没利用向量索引，退回关键词检索的老路。
堆 GPU 改善不了全库精排的算法复杂度，成本线性膨胀，仍然追不上 SLA。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — offline precompute plus online query-only encoding plus ANN is the trio that turns millions of docs into millisecond recall.
Re-encoding the corpus online is O(N) full forward passes — exactly what the dual encoder avoids — pushing latency to seconds.
String matching drops semantic similarity and ignores the vector index, falling back to plain keyword retrieval.
More GPUs cannot change the algorithmic complexity of full-corpus re-ranking; cost grows linearly and still misses the SLA.

termDefinitions.term: ANN index / 近似最近邻索引
termDefinitions.meaning: 预存 doc 向量、支持毫秒级近邻查询的向量索引（如 HNSW/IVF）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ANN index stores doc vectors and supports millisecond nearest-neighbor queries (e.g. HNSW or IVF).

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务级别协议，这里指搜索延迟的承诺上限（如 p99 <100ms）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLA (Service Level Agreement) is a committed limit, here on search latency such as p99 under 100ms.

scenario: 你在 DPR（768 维）和 E5/BGE（1024 维）之间选 dual encoder，语料几百万篇要进 ANN 索引。
scenario_en: You choose a dual encoder between DPR (768-dim) and E5/BGE (1024-dim), with millions of docs going into an ANN index.
q: embedding 维度（768–1024）这个数字影响什么、下游怎么用？
q_en: What does the embedding dimension (768–1024) affect, and how is it used downstream?
why: 维度是每篇 doc 向量的长度：768–1024 直接决定 ANN 索引内存（向量数×维度×4B）和每次相似度计算开销，进而影响 query 延迟。比如 500 万篇×1024×4B≈20GB 原始向量，是算索引内存和延迟预算的基数。
why_en: The dimension is each vector's length, directly setting ANN index memory (count × dim × 4 bytes) and per-query similarity cost, e.g. 5M × 1024 × 4B ≈ 20GB of raw vectors.
options: 维度只反映模型训练时长，与在线索引内存和 query 延迟这些服务侧成本无关
维度越高检索一定越准，应无脑选最大维度，因为它几乎不带来额外存储或计算成本
768–1024 指 SLA 规定的 query 延迟毫秒上限，而不是每篇文档向量的长度
是每篇 doc 向量的长度，决定 ANN 索引内存与相似度计算开销，是延迟/内存预算的基数
options_en: Dimension only reflects training time and is unrelated to serving-side costs like index memory and query latency.
Higher dimension always retrieves better, so pick the max blindly since it adds almost no storage or compute cost.
768–1024 is the SLA's millisecond latency ceiling for queries, not the length of each doc vector.
It is each doc vector's length, setting ANN index memory and similarity-compute cost — the base for latency/memory budgets.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个 query/doc 向量的分量个数，常见 768（BERT-base）或 1024。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The embedding dimension is the number of components in each query/doc vector, commonly 768 (BERT-base) or 1024.

termDefinitions.term: ANN index memory / 索引内存
termDefinitions.meaning: 存所有 doc 向量占的内存 ≈ 向量数 × 维度 × 4 字节（float32）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN index memory is roughly vector count times dimension times 4 bytes (float32).

optionExplanations: 误解：768–1024 不是训练时长指标，它是向量长度，直接乘进在线索引内存和每次相似度计算，跟服务成本关系很大。
误解：维度越高不等于必然更准，而且更高维度会让索引内存和计算量同步涨，不是零成本。
误解：768–1024 说的是向量的分量数，不是 SLA 延迟上限，别把维度和延迟指标搞混。
对；这串数字是每个向量的长度，直接决定索引占多少内存、算一次相似度要多少乘法，是定内存和延迟预算的起点。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: the number isn't a training-time signal — it's vector length, and it multiplies straight into online index memory and per-query compute.
Misconception: bigger dimension doesn't guarantee better accuracy, and it also grows index memory and compute — never free.
Misconception: 768–1024 is the vector's component count, not an SLA latency ceiling — don't conflate dimension with latency.
Correct — that number is each embedding's size, setting how much memory the index needs and how many multiplies one similarity score costs.

scenario: 你要选一个 dual encoder 做 dense 检索，候选是 DPR、E5、BGE 三个主流模型。
scenario_en: You pick a dual encoder for dense retrieval among three mainstream models: DPR, E5, BGE.
q: DPR、E5、BGE 在「零样本能力 vs 微调投入」上怎么排？
q_en: How do DPR, E5, and BGE rank on zero-shot ability versus fine-tuning effort?
why: DPR 是双 BERT-base、768 维、NQ 上对比学习，零样本中等但微调投入最低；E5/BGE 是统一编码器、1024 维、大规模弱监督/指令训练，零样本强到 SOTA 但微调更重。核心轴是「开箱强度 vs 需要多少标注去微调」。
why_en: DPR is dual BERT-base with moderate zero-shot but the lowest fine-tune effort, while E5/BGE are unified encoders with strong-to-SOTA zero-shot but heavier fine-tuning.
options: 三者零样本能力相同，只是向量维度不同（768 vs 1024），微调投入也完全一样
DPR 零样本最强、微调也最省；E5、BGE 两项都更弱更费，属于全面落后
DPR 零样本中等但微调最省；E5、BGE 零样本更强，微调更重
BGE 零样本最弱、DPR 最强，三者微调投入按 DPR<E5<BGE 递增
options_en: All three have identical zero-shot ability, differing only in dimension (768 vs 1024), with identical fine-tune effort.
DPR is both the strongest zero-shot and the cheapest to fine-tune; E5 and BGE are weaker and costlier on both counts.
DPR is moderate zero-shot but cheapest to fine-tune; E5/BGE are stronger zero-shot but heavier to fine-tune.
BGE is weakest zero-shot and DPR strongest, with fine-tune effort rising DPR < E5 < BGE.
optionExplanations: 三者维度不同（768 vs 1024）也罢，零样本和微调投入其实差别很大，说「相同」直接错。
说反了：DPR 是零样本中等而非最强，它的优势是微调省，不是开箱强。
对；DPR 微调最省、开箱中等，E5/BGE 靠大规模预训练拿到强/SOTA 零样本，代价是微调更重。
BGE 恰恰是 MTEB 上的 SOTA、零样本最强，说它最弱与事实相反。
optionExplanations_en: Dimensions differ (768 vs 1024), but zero-shot and fine-tune effort vary a lot, so 'identical' is simply wrong.
Backwards: DPR is moderate not strongest at zero-shot; its edge is cheap fine-tuning, not out-of-box strength.
Correct — DPR is cheapest to fine-tune and moderate out-of-box, while E5/BGE buy strong/SOTA zero-shot at the cost of heavier fine-tuning.
BGE is actually the MTEB SOTA and strongest zero-shot, so calling it weakest is the opposite of reality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 稠密段落检索：用双 BERT-base 在 Natural Questions 上对比学习训练的双塔模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DPR (Dense Passage Retrieval) is a dual-tower model of two BERT-base encoders trained contrastively on Natural Questions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用大规模弱监督对比学习训练、query/passage 加前缀的统一编码器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: E5 is a unified encoder trained with large-scale weakly-supervised contrastive learning, using query/passage prefixes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 智源通用嵌入：用 RetroMAE + 指令微调训练，MTEB 榜单 SOTA。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BGE (BAAI General Embedding) is trained with RetroMAE plus instruction tuning and is SOTA on MTEB.

termDefinitions.meaning: 大规模文本嵌入基准，综合评测嵌入模型的检索/聚类等能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MTEB (Massive Text Embedding Benchmark) broadly evaluates embedding models on retrieval, clustering, and more.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不做领域微调，直接开箱使用的检索效果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Zero-shot is retrieval quality out of the box without any domain fine-tuning.

scenario: 垂直领域搜索（如电商），你手里有大量领域内标注的 query-doc 相关性数据，想最省事地训到强效果。
scenario_en: For a vertical search (e.g. e-commerce) you have abundant in-domain labeled query-doc relevance data and want the cheapest path to strong results.
q: 有充足领域标注数据时，dual encoder 该选哪个？
q_en: With abundant in-domain labeled data, which dual encoder should you pick?
why: 有充足领域标注就选 DPR：它最简单、微调最快就能到强效果，标注正好补上它零样本中等的短板。E5/BGE 的价值是缺标注时的开箱强，此时用不上它们更重的预训练优势。
why_en: With plenty of labels, pick DPR: it is simplest and fastest to fine-tune to strong results, and the labels cover its moderate zero-shot.
tradeoff: DPR（充足标注下微调最省最快）vs E5/BGE（缺标注时零样本更强）
whenOtherWins: 若几乎没有领域标注、又要马上有可用效果，就选 E5 或 BGE——它们零样本就强/SOTA，不靠你补标注。
options: DPR：最简单、微调最快到强效果，充足标注正好喂满它
E5：零样本就 SOTA，有没有标注都无所谓，直接开箱
BGE：微调投入最低，标注多时训得最省
三者随便选，标注数据量不影响 encoder 选型
options_en: DPR: simplest and fastest to fine-tune to strong results, and abundant labels feed it fully.
E5: it is SOTA zero-shot, so labels don't matter — just use it out of the box.
BGE: it has the lowest fine-tune effort, so it trains cheapest when labels are plentiful.
Pick any of the three; the amount of labeled data does not affect encoder choice.
optionExplanations: 对；标注充足时训练成本比开箱强度更重要，DPR 双 BERT 结构简单、收敛快，是最省的一条路。
E5 的强项是缺标注时的零样本，有大量标注时它更重的预训练优势用不上，属于杀鸡用牛刀。
记反了：BGE 微调投入其实最高（中高），不是最低，标注多也不是它最省。
encoder 选型恰恰主要由「标注多不多」驱动，说不影响等于放弃了本题核心判据。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — with plenty of labels, training cost matters more than out-of-the-box strength, and DPR's simple two-BERT setup converges fastest.
E5's strength is zero-shot when labels are scarce; with plenty of labels its heavier pretraining edge goes unused — overkill.
Backwards: BGE actually has the highest fine-tune effort (medium-high), not the lowest, and isn't cheapest with many labels.
Encoder choice is mainly driven by how much labeled data you have, so 'no effect' discards this card's core criterion.

termDefinitions.meaning: 双 BERT-base 双塔，微调投入低、零样本中等。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DPR (Dense Passage Retrieval) is a dual BERT-base tower, low fine-tune effort and moderate zero-shot.

termDefinitions.meaning: 统一编码器系列，零样本强到 SOTA，缺标注时更划算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: E5/BGE are unified-encoder models with strong-to-SOTA zero-shot, best when labels are scarce.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为达到强检索效果需要的标注量与训练成本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fine-tune effort is the labeling volume and training cost needed to reach strong retrieval quality.

scenario: 训练 dual encoder 做对比学习时，要给每个正样本配「难负样本」——看着像相关、其实不相关的文档。
scenario_en: Training a dual encoder contrastively needs hard negatives for each positive — docs that look relevant but are not.
q: DPR/E5/BGE 分别怎么挖 hard negatives，为什么要用难负样本？
q_en: How do DPR/E5/BGE mine hard negatives, and why use hard negatives at all?
why: 难负样本逼模型区分「表面相似但不相关」，比随机负样本训练信号强得多。DPR 用 BM25 挖（关键词像但语义不对），E5 用 in-batch + 挖掘，BGE 进一步用 cross-encoder 挖更难的负例。
why_en: Hard negatives force the model to separate look-alike-but-irrelevant docs, giving far stronger signal than random negatives.
options: 三者都只用批内随机负样本做对比学习，专门挖 hard negatives 对检索训练没有额外帮助
DPR 用 BM25 挖、E5 用 in-batch、BGE 用 cross-encoder 挖
hard negatives 其实指高置信的正样本，拿来直接当标签让模型背下相关性
难负样本只在推理重排时用，训练阶段一律用随机采样的简单负样本
options_en: All three rely only on random in-batch negatives for contrastive training; deliberately mining hard negatives adds nothing to retrieval quality.
DPR mines with BM25, E5 uses in-batch negatives, and BGE mines with a cross-encoder.
Hard negatives actually mean high-confidence positives, used directly as labels for the model to memorize relevance.
Hard negatives are used only at inference-time re-ranking; training always uses randomly sampled easy negatives.
optionExplanations: 随机负样本太好区分、梯度信号弱；正因如此三家都专门挖 hard negatives，说「没帮助」与做法相反。
对；BM25 挖出关键词像但不相关的、cross-encoder 挖出更刁钻的负例，越难越逼模型学细粒度语义。
弄反了：hard negatives 是难的负样本不是正样本，作用是提供强对比信号而非背答案。
难负样本是训练期的对比信号，推理时无所谓正负，说反了阶段。
optionExplanations_en: Random negatives are too easy and give weak gradients; that's exactly why all three mine hard negatives, so 'no help' contradicts their design.
Correct — BM25 surfaces keyword-similar-but-irrelevant docs and a cross-encoder mines trickier ones; harder negatives force finer semantics.
Backwards: hard negatives are hard negative examples, not positives, providing strong contrast rather than answers to memorize.
Hard negatives are a training-time contrast signal; at inference positive/negative is moot, so the stage is reversed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 与 query 表面相似但实际不相关的文档，用作对比学习里最有信息量的负例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hard negatives are docs that look similar to the query but are actually irrelevant, the most informative negatives in contrastive learning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把同一 batch 里其他样本的 doc 当作当前 query 的负样本，省去额外挖掘。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In-batch negatives reuse other samples' docs in the same batch as negatives, avoiding extra mining.

termDefinitions.meaning: 拉近正样本对、推远负样本对的训练方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Contrastive learning pulls positive pairs together and pushes negative pairs apart.

scenario: 你的 dense 检索在语义相近 query 上表现好，但用户搜稀有 SKU 编号、错误码、生僻专名时经常搜不到。
scenario_en: Your dense retrieval works on semantically similar queries but often fails on rare SKUs, error codes, and uncommon proper nouns.
q: dense 检索为什么会漏掉精确关键词匹配，怎么补？
q_en: Why does dense retrieval miss exact keyword matches, and how do you fix it?
why: dense 向量擅长语义相似，但会把稀有 token（SKU、错误码、生僻专名）压进模糊语义空间，精确匹配反而丢了；BM25 这类稀疏检索对精确词命中天然强。所以并行跑 BM25 + dual encoder，融合两路取长补短。
why_en: Dense vectors blur rare tokens into fuzzy semantic space and lose exact matches, while BM25 nails exact terms, so you run both in parallel and fuse.
diagram:
flowchart LR Q["query"] --> D["dense 稠密
语义相似"] Q --> B["BM25 稀疏
精确关键词"] D --> F["融合候选"] B --> F F --> R["re-ranker"]
options: dense 检索本来就覆盖精确关键词，搜不到只说明 ANN 索引没建好
应该彻底换成 BM25，语义检索没有价值，dense 可以删掉
dense 擅长语义但漏精确词，并行加 BM25 抓关键词后融合两路
把 embedding 维度从 768 调到 1024，就能解决所有精确关键词漏召回
options_en: Dense retrieval already covers exact keywords; a miss just means the ANN index was built wrong.
Switch entirely to BM25 — semantic retrieval has no value, so drop dense.
Dense is strong on semantics but misses exact terms, so run BM25 in parallel and fuse both lists.
Raising the embedding dimension from 768 to 1024 fixes every exact-keyword miss.
optionExplanations: 不是索引问题：稀有 token 被稠密向量抹成模糊语义，本质上就召不回精确匹配，重建索引也没用。
全换 BM25 会丢掉语义泛化（同义、改写查询），两者是互补不是替代。
对；dense 管语义、BM25 管精确词，hybrid 并行融合让稀有 SKU/错误码也能命中。
加维度提升的是语义容量，补不了「精确 token 匹配」这个稀疏检索才擅长的能力。
optionExplanations_en: Not an index bug: rare tokens get blurred into fuzzy semantics, so exact matches truly can't be recalled — rebuilding won't help.
Going all-BM25 loses semantic generalization (synonyms, paraphrases); the two are complementary, not substitutes.
Correct — dense handles semantics, BM25 handles exact terms, and hybrid fusion lets rare SKUs/error codes hit.
More dimensions add semantic capacity but can't supply exact-token matching, which is sparse retrieval's job.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按关键词词频匹配打分，对精确 token（SKU、错误码、专名）命中很强。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BM25 (Best Matching 25) sparse retrieval scores keyword frequency and excels at exact tokens like SKUs and error codes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 库存单位编号，电商里每个具体商品的唯一编码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) is the unique code identifying a specific product in commerce.

termDefinitions.meaning: 并行跑稀疏（BM25）+ 稠密（dual encoder）两路，融合候选再精排。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hybrid retrieval runs sparse (BM25) and dense (dual encoder) in parallel and fuses candidates before re-ranking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻检索，用 HNSW/IVF 等索引在百万级向量里毫秒取回近邻，牺牲一点精确度换速度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) search uses an index like HNSW or IVF to fetch close vectors in milliseconds, trading a little exactness for speed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把文本压成一个固定长度的稠密向量，语义相近的文本在向量空间里距离更近。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding is a fixed-length dense vector for a piece of text, where semantically similar texts land close together.

scenario: 你想把 BM25 分和 dense 余弦分直接相加融合候选。BM25 从 0 到任意大（跟词频走），dense 余弦在 [−1,1]。
scenario_en: You try to fuse by directly adding BM25 and dense cosine scores. BM25 ranges 0 to arbitrarily large (term frequency); dense cosine is in [−1,1].
q: 为什么 BM25 分和 dense 分「直接相加」融合会失败？
q_en: Why does directly adding BM25 and dense scores fail as a fusion method?
why: 两个分布尺度根本不同——BM25 无上界（词频越高越大），dense 余弦夹在 [−1,1]。直接相加让数值天生更大的 BM25 主导融合分，dense 信号被淹没，等于没融合。要么按 rank 融合（RRF），要么先归一化再加权。
why_en: The two score distributions have different scales — BM25 is unbounded, dense cosine sits in [−1,1] — so adding them lets BM25's larger raw numbers dominate.
options: 直接相加没问题，两个分数本来就在同一尺度上，融合结果可靠不用处理
失败是因为 dense 分太大，会盖过 BM25，应给 dense 乘小系数
因为 BM25 和 dense 测的是同一件事，相加等于把同一个信号重复计分
两个分布尺度不可比：BM25 无上界会主导，dense 的 [−1,1] 被淹没
options_en: Adding directly is fine — both scores already live on the same scale, so the fused result is reliable as is.
It fails because dense scores are too large and swamp BM25, so multiply dense by a small factor.
Because BM25 and dense measure the same thing, adding them double-counts one signal.
The two score scales are not comparable: unbounded BM25 dominates while dense's [−1,1] is drowned out.
optionExplanations: 恰恰不在同一尺度：一个无上界、一个夹在 [−1,1]，直接相加不可靠，这正是本题要否定的。
大小说反了：是 BM25 无上界会盖过 dense，不是 dense 盖过 BM25。
两者测的不是同一件事（精确词 vs 语义），问题在尺度不可比，不是重复计分。
对；尺度不可比让原始数值大的 BM25 主导，dense 信号被淹没，必须靠 RRF 或归一化加权解决。
optionExplanations_en: They are precisely not on the same scale — one unbounded, one in [−1,1] — so adding is unreliable, which is what this card rejects.
The magnitudes are reversed: unbounded BM25 swamps dense, not the other way around.
They measure different things (exact terms vs semantics); the problem is incomparable scale, not double-counting.
Correct — incomparable scales let the larger raw BM25 dominate and drown dense, which RRF or normalized weighting must fix.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把不同尺度的分数映射到可比区间（如 per-query min-max）再融合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Normalization maps differently-scaled scores into a comparable range (e.g. per-query min-max) before fusing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两向量夹角余弦，取值 [−1,1]，是 dense 检索的相关性分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cosine similarity is the cosine of the angle between two vectors, in [−1,1], the dense-retrieval relevance score.

scenario: 你要融合 BM25 和 dense 两路候选，又不想处理两个分数尺度不同的归一化麻烦。
scenario_en: You want to fuse BM25 and dense candidates without dealing with the normalization headache of two different score scales.
q: RRF（Reciprocal Rank Fusion）是怎么融合两路候选的？
q_en: How does RRF (Reciprocal Rank Fusion) fuse two candidate lists?
why: RRF 只看 rank 不看原始分：每篇 doc 在每一路的得分是 1/(k+rank)，k≈60，把两路相加。因为用排名而非分数，天然绕开尺度不可比问题，无需归一化、无学习参数，是 Elasticsearch/Vespa 的强基线。
why_en: RRF scores each doc 1/(k+rank) per list with k≈60 and sums both, using ranks not raw scores so it sidesteps scale mismatch with no normalization or learned params.
options: 每篇 doc 在每路按 1/(k+rank) 打分（k≈60）后相加，只看 rank
把 BM25 和 dense 的原始分直接相加，谁的数值大就让谁排前面
用点击数据学一个权重 α，归一化后按 α·dense+(1−α)·sparse 融合
只取 dense 一路的 top 结果，BM25 只在 dense 为空时兜底
options_en: Score each doc 1/(k+rank) per list (k≈60) and sum, using ranks not raw scores.
Add the raw BM25 and dense scores directly and let whichever number is bigger rank first.
Learn a weight α from click data and fuse as α·dense + (1−α)·sparse after normalization.
Take only the dense list's top results, using BM25 only as a fallback when dense is empty.
optionExplanations: 对；1/(k+rank) 让排名靠前的 doc 得分高，k≈60 压平头部差距；只用 rank 就绕开了尺度不可比，零参数、零归一化。
直接相加原始分正是 RRF 要避免的尺度陷阱，BM25 无上界会主导。
那是 learned weighted fusion（学权重），需要点击数据和维护，不是无参数的 RRF。
dense 兜底式串联不是融合，会漏掉 BM25 独有的精确匹配候选。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — 1/(k+rank) rewards top-ranked docs, k≈60 flattens head gaps, and using only ranks sidesteps scale mismatch with zero params and no normalization.
Adding raw scores is exactly the scale trap RRF avoids; unbounded BM25 would dominate.
That is learned weighted fusion, which needs click data and maintenance — not parameter-free RRF.
Chaining dense with a BM25 fallback isn't fusion and misses BM25's unique exact-match candidates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 倒数排名融合：按 1/(k+rank) 用排名而非分数融合多路候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RRF (Reciprocal Rank Fusion) fuses multiple candidate lists by rank via 1/(k+rank), not by raw score.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一篇 doc 在某一路结果里的名次（第 1、第 2…）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rank is a doc's position within one list (1st, 2nd, ...).

termDefinitions.meaning: 平滑常数，常取 60，越大越压平头部名次之间的得分差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The RRF constant k, typically 60, is a smoothing term; larger k flattens score gaps between top ranks.

scenario: 你希望融合能「看 query 意图」：关键词型 query 多信 BM25，语义型 query 多信 dense。
scenario_en: You want fusion to read query intent: trust BM25 more on keyword queries, dense more on semantic ones.
q: learned weighted fusion 怎么做，比 RRF 多了什么能力和代价？
q_en: How does learned weighted fusion work, and what ability and cost does it add over RRF?
why: 先把两路分数归一化，再按 α·dense+(1−α)·sparse 加权，α 从点击数据或 NDCG 调出。它能按 query 意图调权，代价是要数据和长期维护。
why_en: Normalize each list then weight α·dense + (1−α)·sparse with α learned from clicks or tuned on held-out NDCG, adapting to intent at the cost of data and maintenance.
options: 和 RRF 完全一样，只是换了个名字，既没有额外能力也没有额外代价
归一化后按 α·dense+(1−α)·sparse 加权，α 从点击/NDCG 学出来
直接相加两路原始分，既不归一化也不学权重，实现起来最省事
用 cross-encoder 把两路候选全部重新编码后直接取平均分，完全不需要学权重参数
options_en: Exactly the same as RRF under a different name, with no extra ability and no extra cost.
Normalize, then weight α·dense + (1−α)·sparse with α learned from clicks or NDCG.
Add the two raw score lists directly, with no normalization and no learned weights — the least effort.
Re-encode all candidates from both lists with a cross-encoder and directly average the scores, needing no learned weight parameter at all.
optionExplanations: 关键差别在于 learned fusion 有可学的权重 α、能适配 query 意图，RRF 没有，说「一样」抹掉了这道题核心。
对；归一化解决尺度、α 让它按 query 意图在 BM25 和 dense 间调配，代价是要点击数据 + 调参 + 维护。
直接相加不归一化正是尺度陷阱；learned fusion 恰恰先归一化再加权。
cross-encoder 重编码是第二阶段精排的活，不是第一阶段两路融合的做法。
optionExplanations_en: The key difference is learned fusion's tunable α that adapts to intent, which RRF lacks, so 'the same' erases this card's point.
Correct — normalization fixes scale and α reallocates between BM25 and dense by intent, costing click data, tuning, and maintenance.
Adding raw scores unnormalized is the scale trap; learned fusion instead normalizes first, then weights.
Cross-encoder re-encoding is a second-stage re-ranking job, not first-stage two-list fusion.

termDefinitions.term: learned weighted fusion / 学习加权融合
termDefinitions.meaning: 归一化后按 α·dense+(1−α)·sparse 融合，α 由数据学出。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Learned weighted fusion normalizes then fuses as α·dense + (1−α)·sparse, with α learned from data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 归一化折损累积增益，衡量排序质量，越靠前的相关结果贡献越大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain) measures ranking quality, weighting relevant results higher when ranked earlier.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户点了哪些结果的日志，用来学融合权重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Click-through data logs which results users clicked, used to learn fusion weights.

scenario: 你要在 RRF 和 learned weighted fusion 之间给 hybrid 检索选融合策略。
scenario_en: You must pick a fusion strategy for hybrid retrieval between RRF and learned weighted fusion.
q: RRF 和 learned weighted fusion 差在哪一维？
q_en: On what dimension do RRF and learned weighted fusion differ?
why: 取舍轴是「鲁棒零参数 vs 适配 query 意图」。RRF 只按 rank、开箱稳但分不出意图；learned fusion 能调权，代价是点击数据、调参和维护。
why_en: The axis is robust-and-parameter-free versus intent-adaptive: RRF is fixed by rank and can't adapt, while learned fusion adapts to intent but needs data and upkeep.
tradeoff: RRF（零参数、鲁棒、不适配意图）vs learned fusion（适配 query 意图，但要数据+维护）
options: 两者都需要点击数据训练权重，区别只是融合公式的写法不同
RRF 能按 query 意图动态调权，learned fusion 反而不能，二者说反了
RRF 无参数按 rank、稳但不适配意图；learned fusion 能调权但要数据
learned fusion 一定更好，RRF 已被淘汰，现在没有任何使用场景
options_en: Both need click data to train weights, differing only in how the fusion formula is written.
RRF dynamically adapts weights to query intent while learned fusion cannot — the two are reversed.
RRF is parameter-free by rank and robust but intent-blind; learned fusion adapts but needs data.
Learned fusion is always better and RRF is obsolete, with no remaining use case.
optionExplanations: RRF 恰恰不需要训练数据（纯按 rank），说两者都要数据是错的。
说反了：能按意图调权的是 learned fusion，RRF 是固定的无参数规则。
对；这就是取舍轴——RRF 拿鲁棒零维护换掉适配能力，learned fusion 拿维护成本换意图适配。
RRF 是 Elasticsearch/Vespa 的强基线、零维护，缺数据或求稳时反而更合适，没被淘汰。
optionExplanations_en: RRF needs no training data (pure rank), so claiming both need data is wrong.
Reversed: learned fusion is the intent-adaptive one; RRF is a fixed parameter-free rule.
Correct — that's the tradeoff axis: RRF trades adaptivity for robust zero-maintenance, learned fusion trades maintenance for intent adaptivity.
RRF is a strong zero-maintenance baseline in Elasticsearch/Vespa, better when data is scarce or robustness matters — not obsolete.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 1/(k+rank) 用排名融合，无参数、无需归一化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RRF (Reciprocal Rank Fusion) fuses by rank via 1/(k+rank), parameter-free and needing no normalization.

termDefinitions.term: learned weighted fusion / 学习加权融合
termDefinitions.meaning: 归一化后按 α·dense+(1−α)·sparse 融合，α 从数据学，能适配意图。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Learned weighted fusion fuses as α·dense + (1−α)·sparse with α learned from data, adapting to intent.

termDefinitions.meaning: query 偏关键词型还是语义型，决定该多信 BM25 还是 dense。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Query intent is whether a query is keyword-heavy or semantic, deciding whether to trust BM25 or dense more.

scenario: 你在搭新搜索系统的 hybrid 融合，暂时没有点击日志，团队也没人力长期调权重，但要马上上线一个稳版本。
scenario_en: You're building hybrid fusion for a new search system with no click logs yet and no staffing to tune weights long-term, but need a stable version live now.
q: 没有点击数据、要快速上线一个稳基线，该选哪种融合？
q_en: With no click data and a need to ship a stable baseline fast, which fusion do you pick?
why: 选 RRF：无参数、只按 rank、不用归一化和标注，开箱就是强基线，正好匹配「没数据没人力维护」。等积累了点击数据、也有资源维护，再升级到 learned fusion 按意图调权。
why_en: Pick RRF: parameter-free, rank-based, no normalization or labels, a strong baseline out of the box that fits 'no data, no maintenance staff.'
tradeoff: RRF（零数据零维护、稳）vs learned fusion（要数据要维护、能适配意图）
whenOtherWins: 当你已有充足点击数据、且 query 意图差异大（关键词型 vs 语义型混杂），learned weighted fusion 能按意图调权，效果超过固定的 RRF。
options: learned weighted fusion：先花两周收点击数据训 α，再上线
RRF：无参数、按 rank、不用归一化，开箱即是强稳基线
直接相加 BM25 和 dense 原始分，最省事
只用 dense 一路，等有数据再考虑融合
options_en: Learned weighted fusion: spend two weeks collecting click data to train α, then ship.
RRF: parameter-free, rank-based, no normalization — a strong stable baseline out of the box.
Just add BM25 and dense raw scores directly — the least effort.
Use only the dense list and consider fusion once you have data.
optionExplanations: 没数据、没维护人力时先训 α 是本末倒置，上线被拖两周还没人长期调。
对；RRF 零参数零维护、开箱稳，正好配「没数据没人力还要快上线」的约束。
直接相加会踩 BM25 无上界主导的尺度陷阱，不是「稳基线」。
只用 dense 会漏精确关键词（SKU/错误码），放弃了 hybrid 的核心收益。
optionExplanations_en: Training α first with no data or maintenance staff is backwards — it delays launch two weeks with nobody to tune it long-term.
Correct — RRF is zero-parameter, zero-maintenance, and stable out of the box, matching 'no data, no staff, ship fast.'
Adding raw scores hits the scale trap where unbounded BM25 dominates — not a stable baseline.
Dense-only misses exact keywords (SKUs/error codes), throwing away hybrid's core benefit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 1/(k+rank) 用排名融合，无参数、开箱稳。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RRF (Reciprocal Rank Fusion) fuses by rank via 1/(k+rank), parameter-free and stable out of the box.

termDefinitions.term: learned weighted fusion / 学习加权融合
termDefinitions.meaning: 归一化后按 α·dense+(1−α)·sparse 融合，α 从点击数据学，能适配意图但要维护。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Learned weighted fusion fuses as α·dense + (1−α)·sparse with α learned from clicks, adapting to intent but needing maintenance.

scenario: hybrid 融合后的候选集要交给 cross-encoder 精排；融合候选通常在 100–1000 篇量级。
scenario_en: The fused candidate set goes to the cross-encoder for re-ranking; fused candidates are typically 100–1000 docs.
q: 「融合候选 100–1000 篇」这个量级下游决定了什么？
q_en: What does the '100–1000 fused candidates' magnitude determine downstream?
why: 100–1000 是第一阶段召回后、进精排前的候选规模，它是算第二阶段成本的输入：cross-encoder 每篇一次前向传播，1000 篇≈2s（超 SLA），所以还要从这里再砍到 20–50 篇才精排。这个数字是连接召回和精排的桥。
why_en: It is the post-recall pre-rerank candidate size and the input to second-stage cost: at ~2ms/doc, 1000 docs ≈ 2s, so you further cut to 20–50 for re-ranking.
options: 是最终展示给用户的结果条数，搜索结果页一次性直接渲染这么多条
是 ANN 索引里 doc 向量的总条数，决定整个索引常驻内存占多大
是召回后进精排前的候选规模，决定 cross-encoder 精排成本
是系统每秒处理的 query 数（QPS），主要用于服务端容量规划
options_en: The number of results shown to the user, all rendered on the results page at once.
The total count of doc vectors in the ANN index, setting how much resident memory the index takes.
The post-recall, pre-rerank candidate size, which sets the cross-encoder re-ranking cost.
The queries per second (QPS) the system handles, used mainly for serving capacity planning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第一阶段召回、进第二阶段精排前的一批文档。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The candidate set is the batch of docs recalled in stage one before stage-two re-ranking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第二阶段精排模型，每个 query-doc 对一次前向传播，成本随候选数线性增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-encoder is the second-stage re-ranker; it runs one forward pass per query-doc pair, so cost grows linearly with candidate count.

optionExplanations: 误解：这是候选集大小，不是最终展示条数——真正返回用户的是精排后的 top 几条，远小于这个数。
误解：向量总量是语料规模决定的索引大小，跟这批融合后候选数是两回事，别混为一谈。
对；这批候选是精排前要过一遍 cross-encoder 的量，数字越大精排越贵，所以还得再砍到几十篇。
误解：这数字说的是候选集规模，不是每秒请求量，QPS 得看流量日志而不是候选数。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: this is the candidate-set size, not what's shown to the user — actual results are the much smaller top few after re-ranking.
Misconception: total vector count is the whole index's size, a different number from this post-fusion candidate count.
Correct — this batch is what still has to pass through the cross-encoder, so a bigger number means pricier re-ranking and a harder trim afterward.
Misconception: this number describes candidate-set size, not requests per second — QPS comes from traffic logs, not candidate counts.

scenario: 第二阶段要对 top-K 候选做最精准打分，dual encoder 因 query 和 doc 分开编码，看不到 token 级交互。
scenario_en: Stage two must score top-K candidates most precisely, but a dual encoder encodes query and doc separately and never sees token-level interaction.
q: cross-encoder 相比 dual encoder 精度更高的机制是什么？
q_en: What mechanism makes a cross-encoder more accurate than a dual encoder?
why: cross-encoder 把 query 和 doc 拼成 [CLS] query [SEP] doc 一条序列过 transformer，token 之间直接互相 attend，抓住双塔分开编码丢掉的细粒度交互。
why_en: A cross-encoder concatenates into [CLS] query [SEP] doc through one transformer so every query token attends every doc token, capturing interactions the dual encoder loses.
diagram:
flowchart LR Q["query token"] --> A["cross-encoder
[CLS] q [SEP] d"] D["doc token"] --> A A --> S["每个 q token attend
每个 d token → 精排分"]
options: 拼成一条序列过 transformer，让每个 query token attend doc token
用更高维的向量表示，把 query 和 doc 完全分开独立编码，再用点积算出相关性分数
把每篇 doc 的向量提前放在离线阶段算好存起来，query 到达时只需单独计算一次相似度
先用 BM25 单独算出关键词匹配的分数，再拿它对 dual encoder 已经产出的排序结果做一次二次加权
options_en: Concatenate query and doc into one transformer sequence so tokens attend each other.
Represent them with higher-dimensional vectors, encoding query and doc completely separately, then take the dot product.
Precompute every doc vector offline ahead of time, then compute just one similarity when the query arrives.
First score keyword matches with BM25 alone, then use that to re-weight the dual encoder's ranked results a second time.
optionExplanations: 对；同一序列里 token 互相看得见，比分开编码多抓住了细粒度信号，精度因此更高。
升维还是分开编码（双塔），仍然看不到 token 级交互，改变不了本质。
离线预算加一次相似度正是双塔模型的做法，精度受限的根子就在这里。
BM25 加权是稀疏路子，和 cross-encoder（精排阶段）的 token 交互精排本质不同。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — tokens in one shared sequence can see each other, picking up fine-grained signal that separate encoding throws away.
Higher dimensions are still separate (dual-tower) encoding with no token-level interaction, so nothing fundamental changes.
Offline precompute plus one similarity is exactly the dual encoder, and that's the source of its precision limit.
BM25 re-weighting is sparse fusion, a different thing from cross-encoder token-interaction re-ranking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 query 和 doc 拼成一条序列过 transformer，让 token 互相 attend，精度高但慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-encoder concatenates query and doc into one sequence through a transformer so tokens attend each other — accurate but slow.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分类符：序列开头的特殊 token，其输出向量汇总整条序列用于打分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CLS (Classification token) is a special token at the sequence start whose output vector summarizes the whole sequence for scoring.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分隔符：用来分隔 query 和 doc 两段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SEP (Separator token) separates the query and doc segments.

termDefinitions.meaning: transformer 里每个 token 根据相关性加权融合其他 token 的信息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Attention lets each token in a transformer aggregate information from others weighted by relevance.

scenario: 用 BERT-base cross-encoder 精排，每个 query-doc 对要一次独立前向传播，O(N)。
scenario_en: Re-ranking with a BERT-base cross-encoder needs one independent forward pass per query-doc pair, O(N).
q: 「1000 篇精排 ≈ 2s（单 GPU）」这个数字推出什么设计动作？
q_en: What design action does '1000 docs ≈ 2s on one GPU' imply?
why: cross-encoder 是 O(N)，每对一次前向传播，1000 篇约 2s，是 <100ms SLA 的 20 倍。所以 K 必须砍到 20–50 篇才卡进预算。
why_en: Cross-encoder cost is O(N): 1000 docs ≈ 2s on one GPU BERT-base, far over a <100ms SLA, so cut re-ranking to 20–50 docs (~40–100ms).
options: 说明可以直接对全部 1000 篇都精排，2s 的延迟在搜索场景里用户完全能接受
说明只要换一块更大的 GPU、加更多机器，就能把 2s 压进毫秒，候选数完全不用动
说明 cross-encoder 的成本和候选数无关，砍不砍候选数最后跑起来都一样快
O(N) 下 1000 篇约 2s 超 SLA，需把候选砍到 20–50 篇才够快
options_en: It means you can re-rank all 1000 docs directly, since a 2s latency is perfectly acceptable to search users.
It means a bigger GPU alone compresses 2s to milliseconds, so the candidate count needs no change.
It means cross-encoder cost is independent of candidate count, so trimming or not is equally fast.
Under O(N), 1000 docs ≈ 2s exceeds the SLA, so trim candidates to 20–50 to fit the budget.

termDefinitions.meaning: 成本随候选数线性增长，cross-encoder 每篇一次前向传播。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(N) means cost grows linearly with candidate count, as a cross-encoder runs one forward pass per doc.

termDefinitions.meaning: 图形处理器：跑深度模型前向传播的加速硬件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) is the accelerator hardware that runs deep-model forward passes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务级别协议，这里指搜索延迟上限（如 <100ms）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLA (Service Level Agreement) is a committed limit, here search latency under 100ms.

termDefinitions.meaning: 双向 Transformer 编码器，cross-encoder 常用的底座。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) is the bidirectional encoder commonly used as the cross-encoder backbone.

optionExplanations: 误解：2s 是 SLA<100ms 的 20 倍，用户等不了，这不是能不能接受的问题，是硬超时。
误解：换 GPU 顶多提速几倍，压不掉 20 倍的差距，候选数这一步省不掉。
误解：成本恰恰随候选数线性涨，每多一篇就多一次 O(N) 前向传播，砍候选是唯一杠杆。
对；这数字是定 K 的算式输入——差 20 倍靠加机器补不回来，只能减少送进精排的候选数。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: 2s is 20x a 100ms SLA — this isn't a matter of user tolerance, it's a hard timeout.
Misconception: a bigger GPU buys a few times speedup at best, not the 20x cut needed, so trimming candidates is still required.
Misconception: cost grows linearly with candidate count — each extra doc is one more forward pass, so trimming candidates is the only lever.
Correct — this number is the input for sizing K: a 20x gap cannot be closed with more hardware, only by feeding fewer candidates into re-ranking.

scenario: 融合后有 500 篇候选，SLA 要求 p99 <100ms，单 GPU BERT-base cross-encoder 每篇约 2ms。
scenario_en: After fusion there are 500 candidates, the SLA is p99 <100ms, and a one-GPU BERT-base cross-encoder costs ~2ms per doc.
q: 该把多少候选送进 cross-encoder 精排？
q_en: How many candidates should you send into the cross-encoder for re-ranking?
why: 500 篇×2ms=1s，直接超 100ms SLA。要把精排候选砍到 20–50 篇（约 40–100ms），其余保留第一阶段融合排序即可。K 太小丢召回、太大超时，20–50 是精度和延迟的甜点区。
why_en: 500 × 2ms = 1s blows the 100ms SLA, so cut to 20–50 docs (~40–100ms) and keep the fused order for the rest — the sweet spot between recall and latency.
tradeoff: K 大（精度高但延迟高、可能超 SLA）vs K 小（延迟低但可能漏掉靠后的相关 doc）
whenOtherWins: 若 SLA 很宽松（离线批处理，或秒级可接受的场景），可以精排更多候选甚至全部 500 篇，用延迟换更高精度。
options: 全部 500 篇都精排，精度优先，延迟以后再优化
只精排排名第 1 的那一篇，延迟最低
砍到 20–50 篇精排，其余保留融合排序
精排 300 篇，取 500 和 50 的中间值最稳
options_en: Re-rank all 500, precision first, optimize latency later.
Re-rank only the single top-ranked doc, for the lowest latency.
Trim to 20–50 docs for re-ranking and keep the fused order for the rest.
Re-rank 300, the midpoint between 500 and 50, for stability.
optionExplanations: 500 篇×2ms=1s，是 SLA 的 10 倍，全精排直接超时，不是「以后优化」的事。
只精排 1 篇等于没精排，K 太小会把靠后的相关 doc 全丢掉，召回崩塌。
对；20–50 篇约 40–100ms 卡进 SLA，又保住 top 区精度，是延迟-精度的甜点区。
300 篇×2ms=600ms 仍远超 100ms SLA，「取中间」没有对着延迟预算算账。
optionExplanations_en: 500 × 2ms = 1s is 10× the SLA, so full re-ranking times out — not a 'later' problem.
Re-ranking 1 is effectively none; too small a K drops the relevant docs further down and recall collapses.
Correct — 20–50 docs at ~40–100ms fits the SLA while keeping top-region precision, the latency-precision sweet spot.
300 × 2ms = 600ms still far exceeds the 100ms SLA; 'middle value' never did the latency-budget math.

termDefinitions.meaning: 送进 cross-encoder 精排的候选篇数，是延迟 vs 精度的主旋钮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: K is the number of candidates sent to the cross-encoder, the primary latency-versus-precision knob.

termDefinitions.meaning: 99% 的请求延迟都低于这个值，衡量尾部延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p99 latency is the value below which 99% of requests fall, measuring tail latency.

scenario: 你想要比 dual encoder 更懂 token 级交互、又比 cross-encoder 便宜的中间方案。
scenario_en: You want a middle ground that sees more token-level interaction than a dual encoder but is cheaper than a cross-encoder.
q: ColBERT 的「late interaction / MaxSim」是怎么工作的，代价是什么？
q_en: How does ColBERT's late interaction / MaxSim work, and what is the cost?
why: ColBERT 离线存每 doc 的逐 token 向量，在线用 MaxSim 取每个 query token 与所有 doc token 的最大相似度再求和。比双塔更细，比 cross-encoder 省，代价是索引更大。
why_en: ColBERT precomputes per-token doc vectors offline and scores by MaxSim, summing each query token's max similarity to any doc token — richer than a dual tower and cheaper than a cross-encoder, at the cost of a larger index.
options: 把 query 和 doc 拼成一条序列过 transformer，和 cross-encoder 完全一样
离线存每 doc 的逐 token 向量，query 来时按 MaxSim 求最大相似度再求和
只存每 doc 一个向量，用点积算相似度，和 dual encoder 无异
用 BM25 按 rank 融合 dense 结果，完全不涉及向量交互
options_en: Concatenate query and doc into one sequence through a transformer, exactly like a cross-encoder.
Store per-token doc vectors offline, and when the query arrives take the max similarity (MaxSim) per token and sum.
Store just one vector per doc and score by dot product, no different from a dual encoder.
Fuse dense results by BM25 rank only, with no vector interaction at all.
optionExplanations: 这是 cross-encoder（在线全交互）的做法；ColBERT 是 doc 侧向量离线预算，两者不同。
对；逐 token 向量配 MaxSim，表达比单向量双塔更细，doc 侧还能离线算好，只是每 token 都存向量，索引会变大。
只存一个向量走点积是双塔的做法；ColBERT 存的是每 token 向量，信息比它丰富。
BM25 融合是稀疏路子，跟 ColBERT 逐 token 的迟交互没关系。
optionExplanations_en: That is a cross-encoder's job (full online interaction); ColBERT precomputes per-token doc vectors offline instead — different.
Correct — per-token vectors with MaxSim represent more than a single-vector dual tower, and the doc side can still be precomputed offline, at the cost of storing a vector per token.
One vector per doc with a dot product is a dual tower; ColBERT stores per-token vectors, which carry more information.
BM25 fusion is the sparse path, unrelated to ColBERT's per-token late interaction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 BERT 的延迟交互检索：逐 token 向量 + MaxSim 打分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ColBERT (Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT) is late-interaction retrieval using per-token vectors and MaxSim scoring.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最大相似度：每个 query token 取它与所有 doc token 相似度的最大值再求和。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MaxSim (Maximum Similarity) takes each query token's max similarity over all doc tokens, then sums them.

termDefinitions.meaning: query 和 doc 各自编码成逐 token 向量，只在打分时做 token 级匹配，而非在编码时拼接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Late interaction encodes query and doc into per-token vectors separately and matches tokens only at scoring time, not by concatenation.

scenario: 你在 dual encoder、ColBERT、cross-encoder 三种交互方式里权衡精度、成本、索引大小。
scenario_en: You weigh precision, cost, and index size across three interaction styles: dual encoder, ColBERT, cross-encoder.
q: dual encoder、ColBERT、cross-encoder 在「交互粒度 vs 成本」上怎么排？
q_en: How do dual encoder, ColBERT, and cross-encoder rank on interaction granularity versus cost?
why: 粒度 dual<ColBERT<cross，精度同向增；成本反向：dual 最省、cross 最贵，ColBERT 存逐 token 向量，索引最大。
why_en: Granularity and precision rise dual < ColBERT < cross; cost inverts, with dual cheapest, cross priciest, and ColBERT's per-token storage making its index largest.
tradeoff: 交互粒度/精度（dual<ColBERT<cross）vs 成本与索引（dual 最省、cross 最贵、ColBERT 索引最大）
options: 三者交互粒度和成本完全一样，只是叫法不同而已
cross-encoder 最便宜、dual encoder 最贵，成本从交互多的往少的递增排列
ColBERT 索引反而最小，因为它每篇 doc 只存一个向量
粒度 dual<ColBERT<cross、精度同向升；成本反向，ColBERT 索引最大
options_en: All three have exactly the same interaction granularity and cost, differing only in name.
The cross-encoder is cheapest and the dual encoder priciest, cost rising as interaction drops.
ColBERT's index is actually the smallest because it stores just one vector per doc.
Granularity dual < ColBERT < cross with precision rising the same way; cost inverts, ColBERT's index largest.
optionExplanations: 三者恰恰在交互粒度和成本上层层不同，这正是选型依据，说「一样」抹掉了全部信息。
成本方向反了：全交互的 cross-encoder 最贵（O(N) 在线），单向量 dual 最便宜（离线+ANN）。
ColBERT 存的是每 token 向量不是每 doc 一个向量，所以索引反而最大。
对；精度随交互粒度升、成本随之涨，ColBERT 用「最大索引」换到 dual 和 cross 之间的中间点。
optionExplanations_en: They differ layer by layer in granularity and cost — that's the whole basis for choosing — so 'the same' erases all the information.
Cost is reversed: the full-interaction cross-encoder is priciest (O(N) online), the single-vector dual cheapest (offline+ANN).
ColBERT stores per-token vectors, not one per doc, so its index is actually the largest.
Correct — precision rises with granularity and so does cost; ColBERT spends the largest index to sit between dual and cross.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每 doc 一个向量，点积打分，最便宜、索引最小、无 token 交互。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dual encoder stores one vector per doc scored by dot product — cheapest, smallest index, no token interaction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 逐 token 向量 + MaxSim，精度和成本居中，但索引最大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ColBERT uses per-token vectors and MaxSim, mid precision and cost but the largest index.

termDefinitions.meaning: query+doc 全 token 交互，精度最高、在线最贵、不预存索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-encoder does full query-doc token interaction — highest precision, priciest online, no precomputed index.

scenario: 第二阶段要提精度，但你担心 cross-encoder 对每个 query-doc 对在线全交互太慢，存储预算又有限。
scenario_en: Stage two needs higher precision, but you worry the cross-encoder's full online interaction per pair is too slow, and storage budget is tight.
q: 精排该用 cross-encoder 还是 ColBERT，怎么权衡？
q_en: For re-ranking, cross-encoder or ColBERT — how do you weigh it?
why: 候选已砍到 20–50 篇、要精度天花板 → cross-encoder；要在更大候选上便宜近似、能接受索引变大 → ColBERT。轴是精度上限 vs 在线成本与索引大小。
why_en: For the precision ceiling with only 20–50 candidates and tolerable latency, use cross-encoder; for cheap near-precision over more candidates with a bigger index, use ColBERT.
tradeoff: cross-encoder（精度最高、在线最贵、不预存）vs ColBERT（精度次高、在线便宜、索引最大）
whenOtherWins: 若存储紧张、候选本就很少（20–50 篇）、且要精度天花板，cross-encoder 更合适；ColBERT 的索引膨胀这时不划算。
options: 永远选 cross-encoder，ColBERT 在任何候选量下都没有使用价值
永远选 ColBERT，它比 cross-encoder 又快又准，还能省下索引存储
两者完全等价，随便选一个即可，不存在需要权衡的维度
要精度天花板且候选少选 cross-encoder；要便宜近似选 ColBERT
options_en: Always cross-encoder; ColBERT has no use value at any candidate volume.
Always ColBERT; it is faster and more accurate than a cross-encoder and saves index storage.
They are completely equivalent, pick either, there is no dimension to trade off.
For the precision ceiling with few candidates use cross-encoder; for a cheap approximation use ColBERT.
optionExplanations: 候选量大、存储够、想省在线算力时 ColBERT 很有价值，说它「没价值」太绝对。
ColBERT 快是相对 cross-encoder，但它索引最大、不省存储，「省存储」说反了。
两者在精度上限、在线成本、索引大小上都不同，正是这些维度构成选型权衡。
对；cross-encoder 换精度天花板（贵、候选要少），ColBERT 用大索引换在线便宜的近似精度。
optionExplanations_en: With many candidates, enough storage, and a wish to save online compute, ColBERT is valuable, so 'no value' is too absolute.
ColBERT is fast relative to cross-encoder, but its index is the largest and doesn't save storage — 'saves storage' is backwards.
They differ in precision ceiling, online cost, and index size — exactly the dimensions that form the tradeoff.
Correct — cross-encoder buys the precision ceiling (pricey, few candidates), ColBERT spends a big index for cheap near-precision online.

termDefinitions.meaning: query+doc 全 token 交互，精度最高但在线最贵。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-encoder does full query-doc token interaction — highest precision, priciest online.

termDefinitions.meaning: 逐 token 向量 + MaxSim，doc 侧可离线，在线便宜，代价是索引最大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ColBERT uses per-token vectors and MaxSim with offline doc side and cheap online scoring, at the cost of the largest index.

scenario: 面试官让你用一句话总结两阶段语义搜索的架构取舍。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to summarize the two-stage semantic-search tradeoff in one line.
q: 「取舍三角」里 dual encoder、cross-encoder、K 各扮演什么角色？
q_en: In the tradeoff triangle, what role does each of dual encoder, cross-encoder, and K play?
why: dual encoder 给吞吐（快、可离线+ANN），cross-encoder 给精度（慢、token 全交互），K（精排多少篇）决定你坐在延迟-精度曲线的哪个点。三者拼出「用多快换多准」的取舍三角。
why_en: Dual encoders give throughput, cross-encoders give accuracy, and K sets where you sit on the latency-accuracy curve.
diagram:
flowchart TD T["延迟 vs 精度曲线"] D["dual encoder
吞吐/速度"] --> T C["cross-encoder
精度"] --> T K["K
决定曲线位置"] --> T
options: dual encoder 给吞吐，cross-encoder 给精度，K 定曲线上的位置
三者都只管精度，延迟由硬件单独决定，和架构无关
dual encoder 管精度，cross-encoder 管速度，K 管索引大小
K 只影响索引内存，和延迟、精度都无关
options_en: Dual encoder gives throughput, cross-encoder gives accuracy, and K picks the point on the curve.
All three only handle accuracy; latency is set solely by hardware and unrelated to architecture.
Dual encoder handles accuracy, cross-encoder handles speed, and K handles index size.
K only affects index memory and is unrelated to latency or accuracy.
optionExplanations: 对；把「多快」「多准」「排几篇」拆到三个独立旋钮上，面试里一句话就能讲清这套架构。
精度和延迟正是被架构决策牵动的，不是只靠硬件；否则就不用两阶段了。
角色反了：快而可离线预算的是双塔 dual encoder，慢而 token 全交互的那个才管精度。
K 主要牵动的是延迟和精度（精排几篇），不是索引内存。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — splitting "how fast", "how accurate" and "how many to re-rank" into three separate knobs is what lets you explain this architecture in one sentence.
Accuracy and latency are precisely what architecture decisions move, not hardware alone — otherwise two stages would be pointless.
The roles are swapped: the fast, offline-precomputable tower is the dual encoder, and the slow full-interaction model is what buys accuracy.
K mainly moves latency and accuracy (how many to re-rank), not index memory.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单位时间能处理的 query/doc 数，dual encoder 的强项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Throughput is how many queries/docs are processed per unit time, the dual encoder's strength.

termDefinitions.meaning: dual（吞吐）、cross（精度）、K（曲线位置）三者构成的延迟-精度权衡。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The tradeoff triangle is the latency-accuracy balance formed by dual (throughput), cross (accuracy), and K (curve position).

q: 把两阶段 hybrid 语义搜索的处理流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the processing steps of a two-stage hybrid semantic-search pipeline.
steps: RRF 或加权融合两路候选，合成 100–1000 篇候选集
query 编码器编 query 向量，同时 BM25 处理关键词
按 cross-encoder 精排分返回 top 结果
ANN 取 dense 最近邻、BM25 取关键词候选，两路并行召回
cross-encoder 对砍到 20–50 篇的 top 候选做精排
why: 流程是：先编码 query + BM25 起跑 → dense（ANN）和稀疏两路并行召回 → 融合成候选集 → 砍到 20–50 篇给 cross-encoder 精排 → 按精排分返回。快召回在前、贵精排在后，是两阶段的骨架。
why_en: Encode query and start BM25, recall dense (ANN) and sparse in parallel, fuse into a candidate set, trim to 20–50 for cross-encoder re-ranking, then return by re-rank score.
diagram:
flowchart LR Q["query"] --> E["编码+BM25"] E --> P["并行召回
ANN+BM25"] P --> F["融合候选"] F --> R["cross 精排
20–50 篇"] R --> O["返回 top"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻搜索，在向量索引里毫秒级召回与 query 最近的 doc。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) search recalls the docs closest to a query in a vector index in milliseconds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 倒数排名融合，按 1/(k+rank) 用排名融合两路候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RRF (Reciprocal Rank Fusion) fuses two candidate lists by rank via 1/(k+rank).

termDefinitions.meaning: 第二阶段精排模型，让 query 和 doc 的 token 互相 attend。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-encoder is the second-stage re-ranker letting query and doc tokens attend each other.

q: 补全 hybrid 融合的两条要点：
q_en: Fill in the two key points of hybrid fusion.
text: BM25 分无上界、dense 余弦夹在 [−1,1]，尺度不可比不能直接相加；无参数的融合方法是 {{RRF}}，它按 {{rank}}（而非原始分）打分 1/(k+rank)，k≈{{60}}。
text_en: BM25 scores are unbounded while dense cosine sits in [−1,1], so they can't be added directly; the parameter-free fusion is {{RRF}}, scoring by {{rank}} (not raw score) as 1/(k+rank) with k≈{{60}}.
why: 记住两点：尺度不可比 → 不能直接相加；RRF 用 rank 绕开尺度、1/(k+rank) k≈60、零参数，是默认强基线。
why_en: Different scales mean you can't add raw scores, so RRF fuses by rank with 1/(k+rank), k≈60, as a parameter-free strong baseline.

termDefinitions.meaning: 倒数排名融合，按 1/(k+rank) 用排名融合多路候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RRF (Reciprocal Rank Fusion) fuses candidate lists by rank via 1/(k+rank).

q: 补全 dual encoder 的核心心智模型：
q_en: Fill in the dual encoder's core mental model.
text: dual encoder 用两个 transformer 分别编码 query 和 doc 成同维向量，相关性用 {{点积}}/余弦；doc 向量 {{离线}}预算进 {{ANN}} 索引，在线只跑 query 编码器，毫秒召回。
text_en: A dual encoder encodes query and doc with two transformers into same-dim vectors scored by {{dot product}}/cosine; doc vectors are precomputed {{offline}} into an {{ANN}} index so only the query encoder runs online for millisecond recall.
why: 双塔的两个记忆点：相关性=点积/余弦；doc 向量离线进 ANN、在线只算 query，这才换来毫秒召回。
why_en: The dual encoder scores by dot product/cosine and precomputes doc vectors offline into an ANN index so only the query encoder runs online.

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻搜索，预存 doc 向量、毫秒召回 query 的最近邻。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) search stores doc vectors and recalls a query's nearest neighbors in milliseconds.

scenario: 一个内部工具的搜索，语料只有几万篇，query 量很低，团队想省掉第二阶段精排。
scenario_en: An internal-tool search with only tens of thousands of docs and low query volume; the team wants to drop the second-stage re-ranker.
q: 什么情况下可以只用 dual encoder、省掉 cross-encoder 精排？
q_en: When can you use only a dual encoder and skip cross-encoder re-ranking?
why: 当召回本身已够准、规模小、精度要求不高时，单阶段 dual encoder + ANN 就够，省掉精排的延迟和复杂度。一旦 top 排序质量吃紧（电商、法律检索等对 NDCG 敏感的场景），就需要 cross-encoder 补精度。
why_en: When recall is already good enough, scale is small, and precision demands are modest, a single-stage dual encoder plus ANN suffices, saving the re-ranker's latency and complexity.
tradeoff: 单阶段 dual（省延迟/复杂度，精度封顶）vs 加 cross-encoder（精度高，多一层延迟和成本）
whenOtherWins: 当排序精度直接影响业务（点击/转化、合规检索），top 区错一位代价大，就必须加 cross-encoder 精排，单塔不够。
options: 任何规模的搜索都必须用两阶段，单 dual encoder 在任何规模下都永远不够用
规模小、精度要求不高、召回已够准时，单 dual encoder + ANN 就够
只要语料规模大就该省掉精排，语料越大越不需要 cross-encoder
是否省掉精排只看 QPS 高低，和精度要求、语料规模都无关
options_en: Every search at any scale must be two-stage; a single dual encoder is never enough on its own.
When scale is small, precision demands are modest, and recall is already good, a single dual encoder plus ANN suffices.
As long as the corpus is large you should drop re-ranking; the bigger it is the less you need a cross-encoder.
Whether to skip re-ranking depends only on QPS, unrelated to precision demands or corpus size.
optionExplanations: 系统设计没有「永远必须」；小规模、低精度要求时单塔够用，加精排是浪费延迟。
对；召回够准 + 精度要求不高 + 规模小，单塔 ANN 就满足，省掉精排的一层延迟和维护。
语料越大反而更需要精排收窄，「越大越不需要」把方向搞反了。
是否省精排主要看精度要求（NDCG 敏不敏感），不是只看 QPS。
optionExplanations_en: System design has no 'always must'; at small scale with modest precision needs a single tower is enough, and adding re-ranking just wastes latency.
Correct — good-enough recall plus modest precision needs plus small scale means single-tower ANN suffices, saving a re-ranking layer.
A larger corpus needs re-ranking to narrow more, not less; 'bigger means less needed' reverses the direction.
Whether to skip re-ranking is mainly about precision needs (NDCG sensitivity), not QPS alone.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第一阶段召回模型，doc 向量离线进 ANN，在线只算 query。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dual encoder is the first-stage recall model with doc vectors offline in ANN and only the query encoded online.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量排序质量，越靠前的相关结果贡献越大；对它敏感的场景需要精排。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain) measures ranking quality, rewarding relevant results ranked earlier; NDCG-sensitive cases need re-ranking.

scenario: E5 和 BGE 用「一个统一编码器」同时编 query 和 doc（不像 DPR 用两个分开的塔）。
scenario_en: E5 and BGE use one unified encoder to embed both query and doc (unlike DPR's two separate towers).
q: E5/BGE 用统一编码器时，靠什么区分「这是 query 还是 doc」？
q_en: With a unified encoder, how do E5/BGE tell whether the input is a query or a doc?
why: 统一编码器一套权重编两种文本，靠输入前缀/指令区分角色：E5 加 query:/passage: 前缀，BGE 用指令（instruction）。这让一个模型学到 query、doc 各自该怎么表示，省去维护两个塔。
why_en: One shared weight set embeds both, distinguishing roles by input prefixes/instructions: E5 adds query:/passage: prefixes, BGE uses an instruction.
options: 靠两套完全独立的编码器权重，本质还是 DPR 那种双塔结构
靠文本长度自动判断，长的当 doc、短的当 query，编码器根本无需额外标记
靠输入前缀/指令区分：E5 用 query:，BGE 用 instruction
靠 BM25 分数区分，分数高的那条当 query，低的当 doc
options_en: By two fully independent encoder weight sets — essentially DPR's dual-tower structure.
By text length automatically — longer is treated as a doc, shorter as a query, so the encoder needs no extra marker at all.
By an input prefix or instruction: E5 uses query:/passage:, BGE uses an instruction.
By BM25 score, treating the higher-scoring text as the query and the lower as the doc.
optionExplanations: 统一编码器恰恰是一套权重编两种文本，用两套独立权重就退回 DPR 双塔了。
长度不是可靠信号，短 doc、长 query 都常见，模型无从据此区分角色。
对；前缀（query:/passage:）或指令显式告诉同一个编码器当前在编 query 还是 doc，一套权重两用。
BM25 是稀疏检索分，和统一编码器区分 query/doc 角色毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: A unified encoder is precisely one weight set for both; two separate weight sets would revert to DPR's dual tower.
Length is not a reliable signal — short docs and long queries are common — so the model can't distinguish roles by it.
Correct — a prefix (query:/passage:) or instruction explicitly tells the shared encoder whether it's embedding a query or a doc.
BM25 is a sparse retrieval score, unrelated to how a unified encoder distinguishes query/doc roles.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一套权重同时编码 query 和 doc（E5、BGE），靠前缀/指令区分角色。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A unified encoder shares one weight set to embed both query and doc (E5, BGE), distinguishing roles by prefix/instruction.

termDefinitions.meaning: E5 在输入前加 query: 或 passage: 标明文本角色。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A prefix is E5's query: or passage: marker prepended to indicate the text's role.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向检索的掩码自编码预训练，BGE 用它打底。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RetroMAE (Retrieval-oriented Masked Auto-Encoder) is retrieval-focused masked autoencoding pretraining that BGE builds on.

q: 补全 cross-encoder 的机制和成本：
q_en: Fill in the cross-encoder's mechanism and cost.
text: cross-encoder 把 query 和 doc 拼成 {{[CLS]}} query {{[SEP]}} doc 一条序列过 transformer，让每个 query token attend 每个 doc token；成本是每对一次前向传播即 {{O(N)}}，所以只精排 20–50 篇。
text_en: A cross-encoder concatenates into {{[CLS]}} query {{[SEP]}} doc through one transformer so every query token attends every doc token; cost is one forward pass per pair, i.e. {{O(N)}}, so re-rank only 20–50.
why: cross-encoder 的两个记忆点：拼 [CLS] query [SEP] doc 做全 token 交互（所以准）；每对一次前向传播 O(N)（所以慢、只精排 20–50 篇）。
why_en: A cross-encoder does full token interaction over [CLS] query [SEP] doc for accuracy but costs O(N) per pair, so you re-rank only 20–50 candidates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分类符：序列开头的特殊 token，其输出汇总整条序列用于打分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CLS (Classification token) is a special token at the sequence start whose output summarizes the sequence for scoring.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分隔符：分隔 query 和 doc 两段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SEP (Separator token) separates the query and doc segments.

termDefinitions.meaning: 成本随候选数线性增长，每对一次前向传播。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(N) means cost grows linearly with candidate count, one forward pass per pair.

scenario: 语料 2000 万篇要进 ANN 索引，内存吃紧；你在 768 维（DPR）和 1024 维（E5/BGE）之间选。
scenario_en: 20M docs go into an ANN index with tight memory; you choose between 768-dim (DPR) and 1024-dim (E5/BGE).
q: 内存吃紧时，768 维 vs 1024 维怎么权衡？
q_en: With tight memory, how do you weigh 768-dim versus 1024-dim?
why: 维度直接乘进索引内存：2000 万×1024×4B≈82GB，768 维≈61GB，省约 25%，相似度也算得更快。内存紧且 768 维精度够用就选低维。
why_en: Dimension multiplies into index memory and similarity cost: 20M×1024×4B≈82GB vs ~61GB at 768, ~25% saved, so pick low-dim when memory is tight and 768 is precise enough.
tradeoff: 768 维（省约 25% 索引内存、算得快，精度可能略低）vs 1024 维（精度更高，内存/延迟更贵）
whenOtherWins: 当 1024 维（E5/BGE）带来的召回精度提升对业务关键、内存也扛得住时，高维更值——精度收益盖过 25% 的内存/延迟成本。
options: 内存紧且 768 维精度够用时选 768 维，省约 25% 索引内存
无论内存怎样都选 1024 维，维度越高一定越好，几乎没有额外成本
维度和索引内存无关，可以随便选，它只影响模型的训练时间
选维度只看模型名字，DPR 就一定比 E5/BGE 差，不用算内存
options_en: When memory is tight and 768 is accurate enough, pick 768-dim and save about 25% of index memory.
Always pick 1024-dim regardless of memory; higher is always better and costs almost nothing.
Dimension is unrelated to index memory, so pick any; it only affects training time.
Choose dimension by model name alone; DPR must be worse than E5/BGE, no memory math needed.
optionExplanations: 对；768 vs 1024 直接乘进内存（省约 25%）和相似度计算量，内存紧且精度够用时低维更划算。
1024 维要多约 25% 内存、算得更慢，「没有成本」忽略了 ANN 索引和延迟的真实开销。
维度是向量长度，直接决定索引内存（向量数×维度×4B），说「无关」与算式矛盾。
维度选型看内存/精度权衡，不是看模型名；DPR 低维省内存、微调省，各有胜场。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — 768 vs 1024 multiplies into memory (~25% saved) and similarity cost, so low-dim wins when memory is tight and precision suffices.
1024-dim needs ~25% more memory and computes slower; 'costs nothing' ignores the real ANN index and latency overhead.
Dimension is the vector length and directly sets index memory (count×dim×4B), so 'unrelated' contradicts the formula.
Dimension choice is a memory/precision tradeoff, not a name game; DPR's low dim saves memory and fine-tuning, with its own wins.

termDefinitions.meaning: 向量长度，768 或 1024，直接乘进索引内存与相似度计算量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The embedding dimension is the vector length, 768 or 1024, multiplying into index memory and similarity cost.

termDefinitions.term: ANN index memory / 索引内存
termDefinitions.meaning: ≈ 向量数 × 维度 × 4 字节（float32）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN index memory is roughly vector count times dimension times 4 bytes (float32).

scenario: hybrid 里加 BM25 是为了补 dense 的短板：哪些 query 靠 BM25 才召得回。
scenario_en: Adding BM25 in hybrid covers dense's blind spot: which queries only BM25 can recall.
q: 以下哪些是 dense 容易漏、要靠 BM25 精确匹配才召回的？(多选)
q_en: Which of these does dense tend to miss, needing BM25's exact match to recall? (multiple)
why: dense 把稀有 token 抹进模糊语义空间，精确匹配就丢了——SKU、错误码、生僻专名这类「字面必须命中」的 query 靠 BM25 才稳。而同义改写的语义查询恰恰是 dense 的主场，不需要 BM25 补。
why_en: Dense blurs rare tokens into fuzzy semantics and loses exact matches, so SKUs, error codes, and rare proper nouns need BM25, while paraphrased semantic queries are dense's home turf.
options: 稀有商品编号（SKU）
错误码（如 ERR_0x8007）
生僻专有名词
同义改写的语义相近查询
options_en: Rare product codes (SKUs).
Error codes (e.g. ERR_0x8007).
Uncommon proper nouns.
Paraphrased, semantically similar queries.
optionExplanations: 对；稀有 SKU 在语义空间没有稳定表示，只有 BM25 的精确词匹配能稳召回。
对；错误码是字面 token，dense 会泛化跑偏，BM25 精确命中才可靠。
对；生僻专名训练里少见，dense 表示弱，BM25 按字面匹配更稳。
错；同义改写靠语义相似，正是 dense 的强项，不需要 BM25 来补。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — rare SKUs have no stable semantic representation, so only BM25's exact-term match recalls them reliably.
Correct — error codes are literal tokens where dense over-generalizes, so BM25's exact hit is reliable.
Correct — rare proper nouns are seldom seen in training and dense represents them weakly, so BM25's literal match is steadier.
Wrong — paraphrases rely on semantic similarity, exactly dense's strength, needing no BM25 backup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 稀疏检索函数，按关键词词频匹配，对精确 token 命中强。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BM25 (Best Matching 25) is a sparse retrieval function scoring keyword frequency, strong at exact-token hits.

termDefinitions.meaning: 库存单位编号，每个具体商品的唯一编码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) is the unique code for a specific product.

termDefinitions.meaning: 靠向量语义相似度召回，擅长同义/改写，弱于稀有精确 token。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dense retrieval recalls by vector semantic similarity, strong on paraphrase but weak on rare exact tokens.

scenario: 有人提议直接用 cross-encoder 给全库百万文档打分，省掉 dual encoder 第一阶段。
scenario_en: Someone proposes scoring all million docs directly with a cross-encoder, skipping the dual-encoder first stage.
q: 为什么不能直接用 cross-encoder 做第一阶段全库检索？
q_en: Why can't you use a cross-encoder for first-stage full-corpus retrieval?
why: cross-encoder 必须把 query 和每篇 doc 拼在一起过一次 transformer，无法离线预算 doc 表示、建不了 ANN 索引，是 O(N) 全库前向传播——百万文档要几十分钟，彻底超时。
why_en: A cross-encoder must encode query with each doc together, so it can't precompute doc vectors or build an ANN index — full-corpus scoring is O(N) forward passes, minutes for millions of docs.
options: 完全可以，cross-encoder 精度全场最高，全库直接拿它整批打分精排一遍效果最好
不行，因为它对语义的理解精度太低，全库召回的质量根本不够看，得换别的
query+doc 要拼一起算，没法离线预算或建 ANN，全库 O(N) 前向传播直接超时
不行，因为这个架构完全不支持在 GPU 上跑，只能老老实实换 CPU 慢慢算
options_en: Totally fine — the cross-encoder tops out on accuracy, so running it once over the whole corpus to score and rank directly gives the best results.
No, because its grasp of semantics is too weak and full-corpus recall quality just isn't good enough.
Query and doc must be encoded together, so it can't precompute or build an ANN, making full-corpus O(N) forward passes time out.
No, because this architecture flatly doesn't run on GPUs and is stuck crawling along on CPU.
optionExplanations: 全库要 O(N) 前向传播，跑完得几十分钟，精度再高也先超时，这正是两阶段要避开的坑。
论精度它其实是最高的，问题从来不在精度，而在没法把这套算法撑到全库规模。
对；它得让 query 和每篇文档同序列一起编码，doc 侧没法离线复用也建不了 ANN，只能全库逐对算，超时。
它照样能上 GPU 跑，卡脖子的是全库逐对前向传播这个算法成本，不是硬件支不支持。
optionExplanations_en: Full-corpus O(N) forward passes take minutes, so even top precision times out first — exactly what two stages avoid.
Its precision is actually the highest; the problem was never precision, it's that this approach can't scale to the whole corpus.
Correct — it has to encode query and doc in one sequence together, so doc vectors can't be reused offline or indexed by ANN, forcing pairwise full-corpus scoring that times out.
It runs on GPUs just fine; the real bottleneck is the algorithmic cost of pairwise full-corpus forward passes, not hardware support.

termDefinitions.meaning: query+doc 同序列全交互，无法离线预算 doc 向量，只能精排少量候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-encoder fully interacts query+doc in one sequence, can't precompute doc vectors, and only re-ranks a few candidates.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) needs precomputable doc vectors to build an index, which a cross-encoder can't provide.

termDefinitions.meaning: 成本随文档数线性增长，全库精排即百万次前向传播。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(N) means cost grows linearly with doc count, so full-corpus re-ranking is millions of forward passes.
